title: How to Fake a Sunset When the Sky Gives You Nothing
excerpt: Neil Redfern rescued a gray wedding evening with one gelled flash behind the couple. The trick is two layers: a dark ambient exposure first, then one warm, hard light doing the work of the sun.

title: Can a 2.5-Pound Kit Really Do Wildlife?
excerpt: Hillary K. Grigonis took a Sony A6700 and 70-350mm lens on a 2.5-mile refuge hike. She came back happy, and honest about what the light kit gives up.

title: Wildlife Silhouettes Are About Shape, Not Sunset
excerpt: Kate Garibaldi's guide to backlit wildlife argues the best silhouettes are deliberate: a recognizable outline, a telling posture, and a clean background, exposed for the sky.
